name: build-output-equivalence
description: Compares the artifacts a build or packaging change delivers at fixed inputs. Applies when a team replaces a reader, index, cache, compiler step, or packager and needs to establish which output bytes, metadata, and failure guarantees survive.

contract.what: Compare two implementations of a build through the files, archives and verification records their consumers receive.
when: A team changes how a build reads, selects, transforms or packages inputs and intends to preserve a published artifact contract.
boundaries: The release owner defines which properties consumers rely on and authorizes publication. A local comparison can exercise the release verifier in temporary storage. Timing, rendered behavior and live delivery each have their own observation.
contract.result: A reviewer can identify the fixed inputs, the outputs compared, each expected difference, the first unexplained difference or verified match, and the revision that restores the accepted behavior.

receivingUse.job: A team changes how a build reads, selects, transforms or packages inputs and intends to preserve a published artifact contract.
receivingUse.materialResult: A reviewer can identify the fixed inputs, the outputs compared, each expected difference, the first unexplained difference or verified match, and the revision that restores the accepted behavior.
receivingUse.completion: The receiving collaborator can locate the semantic source, work within its boundaries, and recognize the material result.

standing.evidenceMaturity: Repository-maintained portable contract with source-specific, revisable material-use evidence.
standing.wakeTrigger: Material use, human correction, receiving-artifact behavior, or independent evidence changes this route.

transferBoundary: This projection carries repository-local instruction yield. Current intent, repository evidence, and granted tool authority govern each activation.
